about: The writer typed a request: start --request 'put the ferry lines in idea-tobias'. One unit migrates the swim line to idea-tobias; nothing needs the writer. The log's first line is 'Migration run, started 2026-10-14 15:30.', the next line is 'Your request: "put the ferry lines in idea-tobias"', and 'Nothing needs you.' comes after it.
spec: spec-run-manager.md 02 item 4; 07.3 item 1; 11 Decisions Log item 78
readings: New handled entries follow the ones already there, sorted by note path (as Python sorts strings, so 'Ideas/…' comes before 'brain-dump.md'), then by their place in the note at close. Neither spec nor contract fixes the order, and run-state.json is compared as parsed JSON, so list order counts.
A handled entry's `pointer` lists every destination on the line at close, as paths inside the project.

'Nothing needs you.' follows the request line, so it is the third line, not the second. The runner's nothing_needs_you check reads only the second line, so this case sets it false (the second line is the request) and checks both lines with `contains`. log.json can't check that the request line comes right after the first line.
